assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made it possible to propagate nuclei on forces computed from the electronic structure on the fly, opening ab initio simulation of liquids, solvated ions, proton transfer and reactive chemistry. It is a foundational method of theoretical chemistry whose originality and lasting impact are unambiguous; it sits close to my own field of simulation of reactions in condensed phase.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by exactly two people, so the configuration is clean and fits a two-laureate prize. Parrinello's later metadynamics and ML-potential work is separate and need not be rewarded here.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, thousands of independent applications and numerous derived codes; interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Computational methods have been recognised sparingly since 2013 and 1998, so committee appetite is uncertain.
Whether the committee wants to bundle this with Parrinello's other contributions is unresolved; I have not verified citation details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, by PROTACs and by molecular glues acting on cereblon, converts the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a drug-design principle. It is conceptually new chemistry (induced proximity), originated in the lab, and has produced clinical-stage drugs and a very large field.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glues. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made decisive later contributions, so the three-name limit forces hard choices and the two sub-discoveries may be unevenly credited.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is growing but approved degrader drugs are still few, so the full therapeutic impact is still unfolding; the chemistry and mechanism are well confirmed by many groups.
uncertainties: Credit among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others is contested.
Clinical maturity may be judged premature by some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved delivery of nucleic acids and enabled siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines at global scale. It is a chemistry-driven invention (pKa-tuned lipids, formulation) with enormous demonstrated impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the Vancouver lipid-nanoparticle work, Anderson and Langer developed lipid libraries and ionizable lipid optimisation, and MacLachlan/Hope/Madden contributed key formulation steps. Credit is spread over six names and is genuinely contested; the three chosen are my best guess of the decisive core.
assessment.maturity: Validated by approved siRNA drug and billions of vaccine doses; the 2023 Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification, leaving the delivery side open, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Attribution among Cullis, Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan, Hope and Madden is unresolved.
Possible perception of overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides, born of nucleic acid chemistry, underlies massively parallel sequencing and has transformed biology and medicine. The chemical invention is clear and its impact vast.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry; other credited names (Rothberg, Ju, Mayer) represent parallel or adjacent platforms. A two-person prize is plausible but the platform lineage may invite objections.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with two decades of ubiquitous use and stable interpretation.
uncertainties: Competing claims from other sequencing technologies (pyrosequencing, other SBS chemistries) complicate credit.
Part of the field's recognition lies in earlier Sanger-era prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry brought intact non-covalent protein complexes into the gas phase, giving stoichiometry, topology and dynamics of assemblies including membrane proteins. It is a major analytical tool for structural biology and is solid, well-confirmed chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Robinson and Heck are the most prominent drivers of complexes and membrane-protein native MS; Chait, Loo and Gross made earlier contributions. Fair configuration is plausible but a priority question exists relative to the 2002 electrospray prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature with broad independent adoption, now routine in structural biology.
uncertainties: Possible perception of overlap with the 2002 mass spectrometry prize.
Early contributors' priority is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing of single DNA and RNA molecules produced portable long-read sequencers and a general single-molecule analytical principle. Original and impactful, linking chemistry of engineered protein pores to technology.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed the idea, Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide passage, Bayley engineered pores, Akeson showed the key enzymatic ratcheting. Five credited names exceed three places; I am unsure about the current status of some individuals, which I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Technology is established and widely used, though accuracy continues to evolve; conceptual validation is strong.
uncertainties: Credit among five people is heavily contested and the eligibility of some may be affected by death.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based theory (d-band model, scaling relations, volcano plots) allows computational design of heterogeneous catalysts and is a quantitative bridge between electronic structure and catalytic activity. Importance and originality are high, and the approach is close to the style of computational chemistry I know well.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the clear originator of the framework; Mavrikakis, Rossmeisl, Jaramillo and Scheffler contributed important extensions. A single-laureate or small prize is workable.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and experimentally validated in many cases (HER, ammonia, CO2 reduction), though predictive reliability is system-dependent.
uncertainties: Scaling-relation limitations and the DFT accuracy dependence are well known.
Whether the committee views this as a theory-first prize is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to over 25 percent in a decade, a rare and rapid materials chemistry breakthrough with deep implications for energy.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park, Seok, Snaith and Grätzel drove the solid-state step changes, and Kanatzidis contributed materials chemistry. The allocation is contested and six names exceed the limit.
assessment.maturity: Stability, toxicity and commercial viability remain unresolved, so the recognition may be premature; the efficiency record itself is confirmed.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and lead toxicity are unresolved.
Credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is disputed.
